notes: THIS DATE IS FOMC DAY ONE, and that is the only thing structurally distinctive about it. Derived 2026-09-08 from all 56 posted meeting pairs 2021-2027 (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, HTTP 200, 164,826 bytes, footer 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'): the 2027 panel reads 'April 27-28' with no SEP asterisk, so this print lands on day one and the blackout runs 2027-04-17 -> 2027-04-29 by the Board's own rule (second Saturday preceding the meeting, through the day after it ends). Both derivations match entries this calendar already carries -- fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17 is titled 'FOMC communications blackout begins (through 2027-04-29)' and fomc-2027-04-28 is titled 'FOMC decision (meeting Apr 27-28, no SEP)'. THREE THINGS FOR WHOEVER PULSES THIS ID. (1) DAY ONE IS NOT RARE FOR A MONTHLY EDITION -- IT IS THE MODAL CASE. 17 of 68 post-policy releases were FOMC day one and ALL SEVENTEEN are monthly editions, which is structurally necessary: day-one last Tuesdays fall in Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, quarterly editions fall in Feb/May/Aug/Nov, and the two sets are disjoint. No quarterly edition can ever be day one. This is the mirror image of the fhfa-hpi-2027-11-30 finding that exactly one quarterly edition in the panel sits inside a blackout. (2) THE DAY-ONE FLAG ADDS NOTHING OVER THE BLACKOUT FLAG, AND THE PRINT ADDS NOTHING TO EITHER. Day one against all other sessions looks sharp on term structure (VIX9D/VIX 0.9996 vs 0.9259, p=0.0001, n=45 vs 1,379, seed-stable) but against OTHER BLACKOUT SESSIONS it is null (p=0.5357), and day-one sessions carrying an FHFA release are indistinguishable from day-one sessions without one on all four daily metrics (p=0.5047 / 0.4018 / 0.5365 / 1.0000). Control on blackout membership, not on day one, and do not attribute a day-one session's behaviour to this print. (3) THE CHAIN'S RELEASE COUNT WAS OFF BY ONE AND THIS SESSION FOUND WHICH. FHFA's own report-archive listing carries 67 rows for 2021-01 -> 2026-08 against 68 last-Tuesday slots; the absent row is 2025-01-28. That release DID happen -- fhfa.gov/document/d/hpi/fhfa-hpi-monthly-january-2025 returns HTTP 200 (1,169,929 bytes) and its press release is dated 'January 28, 2025'. It is an archive-listing gap, not a missed release, and it reconciles fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27's 68 with fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26's and -2027-11-30's 67. Any panel built by scraping that listing silently drops one MONTHLY observation.
